2) Are there any jurisdictional constraints for the witnessing (some on‑prem customer sites require only internal staff for certain controls)?

Julie — a couple of licensing and timeline clarifications from legal/ops perspective: 

> On Tue, 22 Mar 2027 at 08:30, rafael_mendes@redwood.com wrote:
> > - Is CardioAI asking for a transfer of runtime artifacts into an escrow deposit, or only a witnessed snapshot and signed attestation?

To be explicit for redlines: Redwood is comfortable with a witnessed snapshot + signed attestation and the option for a sealed escrow deposit only if CardioAI provides the escrow agent details and accepts the associated transfer and custody carve‑outs in the MSA addendum. If CardioAI prefers escrow deposit, we need to add exhibit text that limits Redwood’s liability during custody transfer.

Also: the license scope language CardioAI requested (residency & operator access limits) is fine but legal asks that the MSA include a short definition of "witnessing" (what Redwood is permitted to do during the window) — e.g., runbook execution, snapshot creation, logs export. Anything outside that should require a separate written approval.

Action items for CardioAI to make the legal review fast: 
- Confirm whether escrow deposit is required or optional (witnessing only is faster).
- Provide a short list of PII/PHI controls that Marco will need in the evidence matrix (so we can pre‑stage redacted artifacts).

We can aim for a redline back by EOD today from Priyom, and Vanessa will propose candidate calendar windows in a separate note.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
